text:
NextItNet’s foundation is stacked residual causal dilated convolutions; adaptive temporal propagation would extend this backbone. Relevant 2024–2026 mechanisms appear mainly in adjacent forecasting/vision research: [ACNet (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.12038) combines multiple dilation scales with learned sampling offsets; [FADC (CVPR 2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.05369) adjusts dilation using local frequency content; [ARFNet (2026)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0925231226004418) constructs adaptive receptive-field pyramids with dynamic scale weighting. These provide design precedents, not evidence of improved NextItNet recommendation accuracy or guaranteed causal, padding-safe implementations.

Recommendation-specific [HGNCDSR (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1145/3715321) uses feature and instance gates to represent current interests alongside longer-term patterns, but does not establish that gates remove older information. A plausible experimental adaptation is a prefix-conditioned controller inside each NextItNet block: use observed time gaps and embedding changes to control causal convolution taps or select dilation scales. This is a proposed synthesis, not a verified published NextItNet method. Enforce past-only sampling, remask padding after every block, and read the final nonpadding position. To claim exclusion across a detected boundary, block every computational path carrying pre-boundary information; gating only the convolution output leaves residual paths and previously mixed features. Compare fixed dilation, fixed recent windows, static gates, input-dependent gates, and adaptive dilation under matched budgets. Perturb older prefixes while holding recent activity fixed to measure retained dependence; gate values alone cannot demonstrate forgetting. All components can remain jointly trained within one model per category.
